business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition; unitary national system; hierarchy: Political Constitution of 1991, Commercial Code (Decreto 410 de 1971), Civil Code, special laws and regulatory decrees)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement (Colombia, Mexico, Peru, Chile; 2015)
Trade Agreement between the EU, Colombia, Peru and Ecuador (provisionally applied 2013)
OECD Convention on Combating Bribery and OECD membership (2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF creation); Ley 1121 de 2006 (counter-terrorism financing); Ley 2155 de 2021, Art. 55 (amending Estatuto Tributario Art. 631-5 on UBO reporting); DIAN Resolución 000164 de 2021 (Registro de Beneficiario Final and Form 3521); Circular Básica Jurídica - Superintendencia de Sociedades, Circular Externa 100-000005 de 2017 (SAGRILAFT); Decreto 1074 de 2015 (AML/CFT rules for supervised commercial entities); Law 1258 de 2008 (S.A.S. regime)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (confidential filing with DIAN and UIAF; not publicly searchable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation of each foreign corporate shareholder (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal or domestic equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in country of origin (e.g., Companies House, US Secretary of State, Registro Mercantil)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (consular legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing the Colombian representative/incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization + Hague Apostille; certified Spanish translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy and 90-day bank reference/KYC profile of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank and notary public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Tax Residency / Good Standing of each direct shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: In-country tax authority (e.g., IRS Form 6166, HMRC residence certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or certificate-by-competent authority per double-tax treaty protocol

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, shareholders and legal representatives against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UIAF and Fiscalía lists, Interpol Red Notices, Clinton List, and Colombian national PEP/sanctions databases; enhanced due diligence (EDD) is triggered by any PEP, senior foreign official, or prohibited-jurisdiction nexus per SAGRILAFT Circular 100-000005/2017 and Ley 2155/2021; screening results must be documented, retained for at least 10 years, and renewed when ownership changes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) - www.rues.org.co and the virtual services portal (SIVirtual) of the competent Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be declared in Spanish transliteration/orthography; the certificate of denomination and search (certificado de homonimia) is issued in Spanish by the Cámara de Comercio; Latin-script foreign words are accepted only if readily adapted to Spanish pronunciation and not creating confusion with existing registered names; the mandatory corporate suffix is 'S.A.S.' or 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Financiera, Aseguradora, Seguros, Fondo de Pensiones, Fiducia, Bolsa, Valores, Comisionista (prior Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia authorization required)
Cooperativa, Fondo de Empleados, Mutual, Mutualista (prior Superintendencia de la Economía Solidaria authorization required)
Nacional, Presidencia, Ministerio, República, Colombia (prior central-government authorization required)
Salud, EPS, IPS, Clínica, Hospital (prior Ministry of Health authorization required for health-service entities)
Policía, Fiscalía, Ejército, Defensa (protected state-security terms)
Any term reproducing or confusingly similar to a registered trademark or protected name (blocked per SIC guidelines)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Rejection due to identical/similar prior registration requires filing a revised preferred name and obtaining a new certificado de homonimia; a one-time extension of the initial 30-day certificate may be granted by the same Cámara de Comercio if requested before expiry; no statutory appellate remedy exists against a registry homonimia rejection, but the applicant may (i) request written justification from the Cámara, (ii) file an opposition claim before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) where a third-party trademark blocks registration, or (iii) re-file with a distinctive element, geographic descriptor, or activity modifier that differentiates the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for low-risk digital retail models: the S.A.S. must state a principal domicile in Colombia (Law 1258/2008, Art. 20) where official and judicial notifications (notificaciones judiciales) can be effectively received; an accredited virtual-office/service-address provider maintaining a physical reception point and mail-forwarding service is generally accepted by the Cámara de Comercio; the virtual office must be located within the territorial jurisdiction of the registering Cámara de Comercio.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated at <10% probability in the first fiscal year). Unannounced on-site inspections are typically triggered only by DIAN tax audits, SIC consumer-protection oversight, or UIAF/SAGRILAFT risk indications; a clear e-commerce/warehouse outsourcing footprint further reduces inspection risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille of shareholder KYC bundle (3 documents: certificate of existence, power of attorney, passport/bank reference)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent apostille authority and notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille fee of USD 15-25 per document at origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of apostilled foreign documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of approx. USD 15-20 per translated page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration of the S.A.S. and registration fee (matrícula mercantil)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Digital certificate (firma electrónica) for electronic filing of incorporation and RUES operations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated trust-service provider tariff for annual digital certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation UBO (beneficiario final) identification and DIAN filing preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; Resolución DIAN 000164 de 2021 obligation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIT and RUT registration for the S.A.S.
Trademark pre-search at SIC for the proposed commercial brand (optional but recommended)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Law 1258/2008 Art. 5 permits private-document incorporation; notarial fees apply only when real property is contributed

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) governed primarily by Law 1258 of 2008, arts. 1, 2, 5, 9 and 25; supplemented by the Colombian Code of Commerce (Decree 410 of 1971), arts. 98-110, 207 and 373-378, and Law 222 of 1995; registration procedure under Decree 1074 of 2015, arts. 1.6.1.1.1 et seq., and the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) regime; foreign investment and exchange control rules issued by the Banco de la República.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), operating through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES); oversight by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private deed of incorporation) executed by all shareholders, filed electronically through the RUES Ventanilla Digital, and recorded in the Mercantile Registry to obtain the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an S.A.S.; subscribed capital and payment installments are freely determined in the bylaws (Law 1258 of 2008, art. 5). No escrow account is required for paid-in capital. Foreign currency contributions must enter through the authorized foreign exchange market and be declared to the Banco de la República on Formulario No. 3 (Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional) within fifteen calendar days of receipt.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. RESOLVED FIRST: That the subscribers' subscription of 100 ordinary shares is approved, constituting the share capital stated in the incorporation instrument. RESOLVED SECOND: That the registered office is established at the address set forth in the bylaws, in [DOMICILE], Colombia. RESOLVED THIRD: That [NAME] is appointed sole Legal Representative (Representante Legal) with the powers contained in the bylaws, including authority to open bank accounts and execute agreements. RESOLVED FOURTH: That [NAME] is appointed substitute representative and [ACCOUNTING FIRM] engaged as independent accountant. RESOLVED FIFTH: That the President and Secretary are authorized to certify copies and file the incorporation before the Chamber of Commerce.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (National Tax and Customs Directorate); operative portals: www.dian.gov.co, MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado), and VUCE – Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior for export-related filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The S.A.S. must obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) by: (1) executing the private incorporation document registered with the Cámara de Comercio to obtain the commercial registration (certificado de existencia y representación legal); (2) completing the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) application electronically via MUISCA using a digital certificate, or physically at a DIAN office; (3) activating the tax profile as 'Responsable de IVA – Régimen Común', 'Obligado a facturar electrónicamente', and 'Importador/Exportador' (as applicable); and (4) appointing a legal representative (representante legal) and, if the incorporators are non-residents, filing a notarized and apostilled power of attorney (poder) with the commercial registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the S.A.S. is a separate juridical person fully liable for corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre la Renta) at 35% on Colombian-source income, with qualifying foreign-source income taxed at the reduced 9% rate (no pass-through treatment; no check-the-box concept exists). The entity is always a VAT responsible person in the Régimen Común; simplified VAT status is unavailable to corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombian law does not provide check-the-box or US-style hybrid-mismatch elections. Available statutory elections include: (i) the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE), an optional consolidated income/VAT/industry-and-commerce tax regime for entities with gross annual income ≤ 100,000 UVT, elected via RUT and irrevocable for a fixed period; and (ii) the Zona Franca regime election for export-oriented operations, yielding a 15% corporate rate and special VAT treatment, subject to prior DIAN authorization. Hybrid mismatch and 338(m)-type classification elections are not recognized.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre las Ventas (Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold applicable to S.A.S. corporations: VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable act. The simplified small-taxpayer category (Régimen Simplificado) is reserved for natural persons with gross assets and income each not exceeding 3,500 UVT (approx. COP 174,296,500 for tax year 2025); a corporation cannot avail itself of this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta – FEV) with real-time 'validación previa' clearance by DIAN. Invoices must be transmitted as standardized XML (XAdES-EPES) through DIAN-approved web services (direct issuance or certified technology provider), bearing the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica), a QR code, and the DIAN validation response ('Validado'/'Rechazado'). Contingency issuance uses the CUDS (Código Único de Documento Soporte). Tax credit notes, debit notes, and the 'documento soporte en adquisiciones' are also filed electronically with DIAN.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and qualifying exports of services are zero-rated (gravadas a la tarifa 0%) under Article 481 E.T., preserving the exporter's right to reclaim input VAT. For physical cosmetics exports, the operation must be evidenced by an accepted customs export declaration and actual shipment abroad. For cross-border digital retail/offshore services, the supplier must evidence that the service is used or consumed outside Colombia and that the foreign buyer receives the benefit abroad; compliance with the foreign-exchange channeling rules is a substantive condition for the zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX) filed through DIAN/Siglo XXI or the simplified export declaration for small-value courier consignments
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical international shipment
Commercial export invoice matching the DEX and the foreign customer's purchase order
Certificate of Forex Reintegration (Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas) or compensation-account declaration issued by a Colombian forex intermediary
INVIMA Cosmetic Notification Certificate (Notificación Sanitaria Obligatoria) together with the export health certificate issued by INVIMA for the consignment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN rigorously audits export zero-rating claims, requiring proof of shipment, the reintegro de divisas, and the service use-abroad test. Failure to repatriate within 180 days collapses the 0% rate, reinstating 19% VAT retroactively with moratory interest. Additional exposure: 'sanción por inexactitud' (Art. 648 E.T.) equal to 100% of the tax understated; 'sanción por improcedencia de devoluciones o compensaciones' (Art. 670 E.T.) equal to 20% of the VAT refund improperly obtained; and, for fictitious exports or forged documentation, criminal tax evasion charges under Article 434A of the Código Penal carrying imprisonment of up to 108 months and fines up to 20,000 SMMLV, with DIAN's assessment window extended from the general three-year term to five years where returns were omitted or fraudulent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia, acting with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia as the supervisory authority for authorized foreign exchange market participants; the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism and the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) also exercise related customs and trade-related foreign exchange functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is fully current-account convertible in the sense that current transactions such as trade, services, royalties, insurance and ordinary remittances may be effected through authorized foreign exchange market participants without prior central-bank approval. Capital-account operations, including foreign direct investment, are also generally open but must be channelled through the foreign exchange market and duly registered with the Banco de la República's international investment registry. Profit and dividend remittances are permitted after Colombian corporate tax compliance; the principal hurdles are corporate income tax at the statutory rate, applicable non-resident dividend withholding tax, the requirement that distributable profits be certified by audited financial statements, and the obligation to demonstrate that the underlying capital was legally registered as foreign investment. Funds remitted to non-residents must be supported by exchange declarations and appropriate tax clearances; no restrictions on dividend conversion exist once the remittance is classified as a lawful distribution from taxed profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exports of goods by Colombian residents must be collected, channeled and liquidated through the authorized foreign exchange market. The exporter must file the corresponding exchange declaration and surrender the export proceeds to an authorized intermediary within the statutory collection window, generally not exceeding six months from the date of shipment for goods; extensions are possible only for justified causes through the handling bank. The mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts is 100% of the collectible FOB/proceeds once received, with only narrow exceptions for foreign currency balances previously authorized or held in permitted foreign accounts. The exchange declaration must be consistent with the DIAN customs declaration, the commercial invoice and underlying shipping documents.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (COP and USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for unlicensed offshore digital EMIs. Colombian regulation confers deposit-taking, credit-granting and payment settlement functions to entities authorized by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia; a foreign digital EMI without a local license cannot lawfully open accounts, process local payments or act as an exchange intermediary. The viable model is to use a locally licensed SEDPE/SVD-enabled payment partner or a regulated digital bank, with Shopify Payments and PayPal employed strictly as merchant acquisition and consumer payment rails that settle into a Colombian corporate bank. If the offshore EMI acts only as a technology vendor and not as a regulated financial intermediary, its cross-border viability becomes medium, but it must not handle Colombian client funds in Colombia without authorization.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In most full-scope commercial banking relationships, at least one natural person must attend the KYC interview at the Colombian branch or before a notary/consular officer, especially when the legal representative and ultimate beneficial owners are non-residents. Colombian AML/KYC standards require the bank to know the customer, the legal representative, the beneficial owner and the intended flows. In practice, the managing director or an appointed attorney-in-fact with apostilled power of attorney, translated into Spanish, must appear for signature registration and identity verification. Some banks permit assisted remote video onboarding for non-residents using biometric verification, but this remains an exception and requires enhanced due diligence documentation; full sub-account or ecommerce-fintech onboarding may be digital, whereas capital account and treasury products mandate physical presence or notarized/consular validation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recent incorporation of a non-resident-owned S.A.S. with no audited financial history or Colombian operational footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and Spanish-translated corporate registration deed and bylaws; RUT certificate; list of directors and beneficial owners; corporate résumé or business plan; parent company audited financial statements for two years where available; lease or service contract proving physical/operational presence; pro-forma expected monthly transaction volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or director identified as a senior political figure or connected to a politically exposed person.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP screening result; notarized declaration explaining source of wealth and source of funds; supporting asset, salary, investment or inheritance documentation; tax returns and prior legal evolution of the capital; formal written confirmation that the foreign investor is not using Colombian financial infrastructure for unlawful transfers; enhanced due diligence questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border e-commerce flows with low ticket amounts and revenue consistency risk, creating unusual velocity patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shopify and PayPal merchant agreements; connection of the entity to the platforms; chargeback and refund policy; transaction reconciliation report; customer acquisition data; IP/service provider evidence; PCI-DSS attestation; AML compliance policy and platform-level KYC/know-your-merchant coverage; direct contractual nexus with cosmetics suppliers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared ISIC activity and banking flows or goods descriptions, triggering classification as an underground e-commerce front.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supplier agreements and purchase orders; commercial invoices from cosmetics manufacturers; freight forwarding and logistics contracts; customs import declarations and DIAN reception notices; warehouse documentation or third-party logistics reports; quality control and product registration certificates if applicable; reconciliation between orders, payments and fulfilled goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sudden inbound capital injection from a related party in a high-risk jurisdiction or through multiple intermediate shell companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder loan or capital contribution agreement; notarial act of capital increase; board resolutions; deposit and wire instructions; Banco de la República foreign investment registration proof; exchange declaration; legal opinion on the corporate chain of the final beneficial owner; source-of-funds banking statements and prior year financial statements of the funding entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from the non-resident shareholder should be executed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT101/MT202 where aggregate transfers are used) directly to the Colombian entity's operational or escrow account maintained with an authorized Colombian bank. Before the transfer, the investment must be registered in the Banco de la República's international investment registry through the local intermediary bank, and the bank must be provided with the incorporation certificate, RUT, board resolutions and proof of UBO. The cash should be denominated in COP or USD; if sent in USD, the bank will convert at the authorized exchange market rate and file the corresponding exchange declaration, specifying the purpose as foreign direct investment. Remittance information fields must contain the entity's NIT, the foreign investment registration code, the descriptive instruction 'Equity capital injection' and the legal expression 'No compensation'. The bank will verify that the sender is identical with the registered investor, that the underlying documentation is consistent and that no disguised loans or false trade transactions are present before crediting and releasing funds for treasury operations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for imported cosmetics inventory and services should flow through SWIFT MT103 for standard supplier payments, with full beneficiary details and commercial invoice references; for larger import orders, an irrevocable confirmed documentary letter of credit is appropriate, transmitted through MT700 and settled against compliant shipping and customs documents. COP payments to local suppliers should use ACH Colombia and PSE rails for treasury efficiency and high-value CUD clearing through Banco de la República for same-day settlement. The entity must ensure that each outbound FX payment is supported by the relevant DIAN import declaration or service contract and is recorded in the exchange declaration filed by the local bank; outbound USD transfers may be settled via the bank's correspondent network, generally through New York clearing in USD or via TARGET2 in EUR. Shopify Payments and PayPal should only be used as customer-facing collection rails; treasury disbursements should be executed through the licensed corporate bank to maintain full FX, tax and sanctions compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Standard deliverable forward contracts on USD/COP with authorized Colombian banks and exchange intermediaries, supported by underlying trade, investment or cash-flow exposure.
Cash-settled forward contracts on USD/COP (non-delivery at maturity) executed with authorized onshore financial institutions, subject to underlying exposure and regulatory documentation.

Plain vanilla USD/COP put and call options with authorized banks for hedging future purchase or sales currency risk; premiums and settlements must be conducted through the Colombian foreign exchange market.
Cross-currency fixed/floating interest rate swaps between COP and USD with licensed local counterparties, used for long-term balance-sheet exposure alignment rather than speculative trading.

Structured risk-reduction products combining plain-vanilla options and forwards, provided the local bank confirms regulatory eligibility, economic hedge purpose and absence of prohibited speculative intent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce of registered address jurisdiction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal accrues the Chamber's non-payment surcharge plus monthly default interest; continued non-renewal over two calendar years triggers administrative cancellation of the commercial registration, barring the company from validly engaging in commercial activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ended 31 December; due between March and April of the following year per the DIAN calendar based on the last two digits of the NIT.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely filing incurs per-month late-filing fines, interest at the current default rate, and possible penalties up to 5% of the tax due; deliberate non-disclosure may lead to coactive collection proceedings and administrative seizure of assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements Deposit (Depósito de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio; Superintendencia de Sociedades when under statutory supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval at the shareholders' annual meeting; meeting must be held by 31 March, thus deposit is due by 30 April of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted deposit permits fines by the Superintendencia de Sociedades, can stop Company certifications, and may be registered as an adverse compliance note.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Informative Return / Exogenous Information (Información Exógena)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the first semester of the following year, generally between March and May according to the DIAN schedule for the reporting entity's NIT ending digits.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or late delivery of the exogenous information is penalized under Articles 651 and 652 of the Tax Code with fines up to 2,200 UVT; inaccurate information attracts an additional fine of up to 10% of benefit obtained.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficiary Confirmation (Información de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual update before 30 June of each calendar year; additionally, any shareholding or UBO change must be updated within three months after the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccuracies in the final beneficiary report may lead to fines of up to 2,200 UVT under DIAN Resolution 000164-2021 and impede the issuance of tax or RUT certifications needed for public contracts and financial operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit (Revisor Fiscal) is required when the SAS's total assets or gross income exceed 3,000 monthly minimum legal wages (SMLMV) at the prior year-end; a lower threshold or audit may be imposed by the by-laws, the sole shareholder, or if the SAS is subject to supervision of the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian Financial Reporting Standards (Law 1314 of 2009, Decree 2420 of 2015): full IFRS/NIIF for Group 1 large entities and NIIF para PYMEs (IFRS for SMEs) for the present online retail SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative must verify and confirm the final beneficiary information to DIAN annually by 30 June; any share transfer must be reflected in the Register of Members at the time of transfer, and changes in natural-person ownership (direct or indirect 5% or more) must be submitted to DIAN within three months.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% for FY2025 (Article 240 ET, as amended by Law 2277 of 2022); no regional surtax applicable to ISIC 4791.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No tax holiday for e-commerce cosmetics DTC; available preferential levers: 250% deduction for qualified science/technology/innovation investments (Art. 158-1 ET), 50% additional depreciation for fixed assets, and VAT on online sales operates outside the income tax base.
